newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut cities get $400,000 U.S. funds.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut cities get $400,000 U.S. funds.

text.p: Hartford and three other Connecticut cities were awarded $400,000 by Environmental Protection Agency to revitalize blighted industrial sites, the state's two U.S. senators said Tuesday.
The other cities are Danbury, Manchester and Meriden.
The funds will help clean up abandoned "brownfield" sites and will also pave the way for new jobs, Sen. Chris Dodd, D-Conn., said in a statement.
Some $200,000 was awarded to Hartford for development in North Hartford and the Sheldon/Charter Oak neighborhoods.
The other three cities will share $200,000.
Danbury officials plan on redeveloping a portion of a former hat manufacturing site, now contaminated with volatile organic compounds, lead and mercury.

"These vacant industrial locations are an obstacle to redevelopment (and) until they are cleaned up they will not be able to attract new businesses, create jobs and add to the community's tax base," Sen. Joe Lieberman, D-Conn., said.
